description.en: Two full-body sessions a week, each with a squat or hinge, a press, a pull and isolation work.
Three full-body sessions a week. Each muscle is trained on at least two days with a mix of compound and isolation work.
Two upper-body and two lower-body sessions a week, so every muscle is trained twice.
Upper and lower days early in the week, then push, pull and legs, so every muscle is trained twice.
Push, pull and legs twice a week. The second rotation shifts the emphasis to other angles and sub-regions.
Two sessions a week with squat, bench press and deadlift in each, one heavy and one lighter exposure per lift.
Squat and bench press three times and deadlift twice a week, each lift undulating between heavy, light and moderate days.

name.en: Deadlift and light squat and bench

description.en: Four sessions with squat and deadlift twice and bench press three times a week, each with a heavy and a lighter exposure.
Five sessions with squat and bench press three times and deadlift twice a week, plus accessory work for the upper back and arms.
Six shorter sessions with squat and bench press three times and deadlift twice a week, for advanced lifters.
Two full-body sessions a week, each opening with heavy competition lifts and finishing with hypertrophy work.
Three full-body sessions a week: each competition lift twice, heavy and light, with hypertrophy work in every session.

name.en: Upper/lower with strength and hypertrophy days

description.en: An upper and a lower strength day built around the competition lifts, then an upper and a lower hypertrophy day.
An upper and a lower strength day around the competition lifts, then push, pull and legs days for hypertrophy.
Push, pull and legs twice a week: the first round built around heavy competition lifts, the second for hypertrophy.
